newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond market sees few trades.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond market sees few trades.

text.p: There were very few trades in the U.S. corporate bond market on Monday, traders said, noting that many players on Wall Street had already begun their holiday vacations.
"The market is dead. Very little or nothing will happen until after the holidays," said one trader.
Traders said prices on high-yield bonds drifted higher by 1/4 to 1/2 a point. Spreads on investment grade corporate bonds were largely unchanged.
Trading in corporate bonds will end at 1400 EST/1900 GMT on Tuesday in an abbreviated session.
The U.S. credit and financial markets will be closed on Wednesday in observance of the Christmas holiday.
As of midday on Monday, the price of the 30-year benchmark Treasury rose 9/32 to 98-29/32, yielding 6.58 percent.
